summary.title: Advice to young web developers
summary.one_liner: A 25-year web developer's opinionated list of principles on server-side rendering, HTML-first design, accessibility, and avoiding anti-patterns like infinite scroll and unnecessary single-page apps.
takeaways: Prefer server-side rendering and plain HTML, since browsers parse HTML faster than JavaScript and HTML already models DOM nodes.
Design for users without a mouse, keyboard, touchscreen, full color vision, or the same information processing style.
Avoid single-page app and infinite scroll patterns unless truly needed; keep the back button and an end-of-content point working.
Always validate data on the server, and treat isomorphic code and client input as a potential security risk.
Code to web standards, test across browsers, use polyfills where needed, and check whether native HTML/CSS (e.g. the View Transition API) already provides a feature.
summary.summary: The author, who has been building websites since 1995, presents a list of unordered tips for younger web developers. The points cover server-side rendering, HTML as the native client language, accessibility for varied input and perception, and criticism of patterns like infinite scroll, habit-forming design, and unnecessary SPAs. An update section adds the back button point, clarifies client-state preservation with fetch() and content replacement, and notes that the View Transition API makes many div-replacement techniques unnecessary. It is opinion and experience rather than a tutorial.
